QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: Other Investment Products_23

question.text: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) mutual funds have a lock-in period of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) are SEBI-categorised diversified equity mutual funds that qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act and carry a statutory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of each investment — the shortest among 80C-eligible instruments. The Trap: A 1-year lock-in is too short for an 80C-qualifying scheme; 5 years matches tax-saving bank FDs and NSC, not ELSS; and 7 years is associated with PPF-related partial-withdrawal/loan rules, not ELSS lock-in. Note: The specific ELSS 3-year lock-in is not stated on the cited NISM Series XVII workbook pages, which support the ELSS/80C tax benefit and reference a 3-year lock-in only in the context of the NPS Tier-II Tax Saver Scheme. The framing above reflects general SEBI MF categorisation and Income Tax Act provisions for ELSS rather than a direct workbook citation.
